events.title: Dangun Foundation Myth
events.description: According to Korean legend, Dangun Wanggeom founded Gojoseon (Dangun Joseon), representing Korea's mythological origin. October 3rd is celebrated as Gaecheonjeol (National Foundation Day) to commemorate this legendary founding date.

events.title: Han Commanderies Established
events.description: Emperor Wu of Han destroyed Wiman Joseon and established four commanderies (Lelang, Xuantu, Zhenfan, Lintun) in northern Korean Peninsula. The Han commanderies strengthened Chinese cultural influence on the Korean Peninsula.

events.title: Silla Founded
events.description: Park Hyeokgeose established Silla (initially called Saro) in Gyeongju. Silla ultimately unified most of the Korean Peninsula, becoming the final victor of the Three Kingdoms period.

events.title: Goguryeo Founded
events.description: Jumong established Goguryeo in present-day northeastern China, later gradually expanding south to northern Korean Peninsula. Goguryeo became a Northeast Asian power, frequently warring with Chinese dynasties.

events.title: Baekje Founded
events.description: King Onjo established Baekje in present-day Seoul region. Baekje maintained close contact with China and Japan, playing an important role in East Asian cultural exchange.

events.title: Buddhism Introduced
events.description: Buddhism was transmitted to the Three Kingdoms of Korean Peninsula through China. Buddhism profoundly influenced Korean art, architecture, literature and thought, becoming a major religion.

events.title: Goguryeo Accepts Buddhism
events.description: Goguryeo received Buddhism from Former Qin, becoming the first Korean state to officially accept Buddhism. Buddhism spread rapidly in Goguryeo, influencing national cultural development.

events.title: Baekje Accepts Buddhism
events.description: Eastern Jin monk Marananta brought Buddhism to Baekje. Baekje later became a bridge for transmitting Buddhism to Japan.

events.title: Silla Officially Recognizes Buddhism
events.description: King Beopheung of Silla officially recognized Buddhism as state religion. Buddhism rapidly developed in Silla, playing an important role in Silla's unification of the Three Kingdoms.

events.title: Resisting Sui Invasions
events.description: Under Eulji Mundeok's leadership, Goguryeo successfully resisted three large-scale Sui invasions. Goguryeo achieved glorious victory at Battle of Salsu, with Sui forces nearly annihilated.

events.title: Tang-Goguryeo Wars
events.description: Tang Dynasty allied with Silla to attack Goguryeo. Goguryeo fell in 668, marking the approaching end of the Three Kingdoms period.

events.title: Fall of Baekje
events.description: Tang-Silla allied forces destroyed Baekje. Some Baekje refugees fled to Japan, influencing Japanese culture.

events.title: Fall of Goguryeo
events.description: Under Tang and Silla allied forces' attack, Goguryeo fell. Goguryeo territory was divided between Tang and Silla.

events.title: Silla Unifies Three Kingdoms
events.description: Silla expelled Tang forces and unified the Korean Peninsula south of the Daedong River, known as 'Unified Silla.' This marked the first substantial unification of the Korean Peninsula.

events.title: Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto Built
events.description: Silla constructed Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto, showcasing superb architectural and sculptural art. These buildings became Korea's most important cultural heritage, inscribed on World Heritage List.

events.title: Goryeo Dynasty Founded
events.description: Wang Geon overthrew the last Silla monarch and established the Goryeo Dynasty with Gaesong as capital. Goryeo is the origin of the name 'Korea.'

events.title: Goryeo Unifies Later Three Kingdoms
events.description: Wang Geon unified the Later Three Kingdoms, completing Korean Peninsula unification. Goryeo adopted Buddhism as state religion while implementing Confucian governance.

events.title: Khitan Invasions
events.description: Liao Dynasty (Khitan) invaded Goryeo three times. Goryeo diplomat Seo Hui skillfully negotiated, and General Gang Gam-chan achieved decisive victory at Battle of Guju, preserving Goryeo independence.

events.title: Mongol Invasions
events.description: Mongol Empire invaded Goryeo six times. Goryeo relocated capital to Ganghwa Island for resistance but ultimately became Mongol vassal state. Mongol occupation profoundly affected Goryeo society.

events.title: Metal Movable Type Printing
events.description: Goryeo invented metal movable type printing, approximately 200 years before Europe. The Jikji is the world's oldest extant book printed with metal movable type.

events.title: Jikji Printed
events.description: Goryeo used metal movable type to print 'Jikji,' the world's oldest extant metal-printed book, predating Gutenberg's Bible by about 70 years.

events.title: Joseon Dynasty Founded
events.description: Yi Seong-gye overthrew Goryeo and established the Joseon Dynasty (Yi Dynasty) with Hanyang (present-day Seoul) as capital. The Joseon Dynasty lasted 518 years, making it Korea's longest dynasty.

events.title: Tsushima Expedition
events.description: To eliminate Japanese pirates (Waegu), King Sejong dispatched Yi Jong-mu to lead forces attacking Tsushima Island. The campaign severely weakened pirate forces, safeguarding Korea's coasts.

events.title: Hangeul Created
events.description: King Sejong the Great created Hangeul (Korean alphabet/Hunminjeongeum), giving Korea a unique writing system. This was a monumental achievement in world linguistic history, greatly increasing literacy rates.

events.title: Hangeul Promulgated
events.description: King Sejong officially promulgated Hunminjeongeum (Hangeul), replacing previous reliance on Chinese characters. October 9 was designated as Hangeul Day to commemorate this event.

events.title: Imjin War (Japanese Invasions)
events.description: Japan's Toyotomi Hideyoshi invaded Korea, sparking the Imjin War. Ming Dynasty China sent troops to aid Korea, and Admiral Yi Sun-sin led the Turtle Ship fleet to glorious naval victories. The war ultimately ended with Japanese withdrawal, though Korea suffered severe devastation.

events.title: First Manchu Invasion
events.description: Later Jin (Manchu) invaded Joseon, known as Jeongmyo Horan. Joseon was forced to establish brotherly relations with Later Jin and pay tribute.

events.title: Second Manchu Invasion
events.description: Qing Dynasty invaded Joseon again, known as Byeongja Horan. King Injo surrendered at Samjeondo, Joseon becoming Qing vassal. This deeply humiliated Joseon.

events.title: Catholicism Introduced
events.description: Korean scholar Yi Seung-hun was baptized in Beijing, officially introducing Catholicism to Korea. Despite Joseon government persecution, Catholicism spread among common people.

events.title: Sinyu Persecution
events.description: Joseon government launched large-scale Catholic persecution, killing hundreds of believers. This was Joseon Dynasty's most severe religious persecution.

events.title: Daewongun Assumes Power
events.description: Heungseon Daewongun became regent, implementing series of reforms to strengthen royal authority. He adopted isolationist foreign policy, strictly prohibiting Catholicism, and closed borders.

events.title: French Campaign Against Korea
events.description: France launched military action against Joseon due to Catholic persecution. Though French forces briefly occupied Ganghwa Island, they ultimately withdrew.

events.title: US Expedition to Korea
events.description: US dispatched fleet to force Joseon to open trade. After Battle of Ganghwa, US forces withdrew. Joseon continued isolation policy.

events.title: Treaty of Ganghwa
events.description: Japan forced Joseon to sign Treaty of Ganghwa (Japan-Korea Treaty), Joseon's first unequal treaty opening country. Three ports were opened, Japan gained trade privileges.

events.title: Imo Incident
events.description: Korean soldiers mutinied, attacking Japanese legation. Qing dispatched troops to intervene, strengthening control over Korea. Sino-Japanese struggle for Korean influence intensified.

events.title: Gapsin Coup
events.description: Progressives led by Kim Ok-gyun attempted modernization coup with Japanese support. The coup failed after three days, reformers fled to Japan.

events.title: Donghak Peasant Revolution
events.description: Peasants launched large-scale uprising demanding reform under Donghak religious banner. Though suppressed, the revolution promoted Korean modernization process.

events.title: First Sino-Japanese War
events.description: Qing and Japan fought over Korean control, Japan won. Through Treaty of Shimonoseki, Qing recognized Korean 'independence,' actually increasing Japanese influence.

events.title: Empress Myeongseong Assassinated
events.description: Japanese agents assassinated Queen Min (Empress Myeongseong) at Gyeongbok Palace, shocking Korea and world. This demonstrated Japan's ambition to control Korea.

events.title: Korean Empire Proclaimed
events.description: King Gojong proclaimed Korean Empire, becoming Emperor, attempting to maintain independence. However, Korean Empire lasted only 13 years before Japanese annexation.

events.title: Russo-Japanese War
events.description: Russia and Japan fought over Korean and Manchurian control, Japan won. Japan forced Korea to sign Eulsa Treaty, making Korea Japanese protectorate.

events.title: Gojong's Secret Envoys to Hague
events.description: Emperor Gojong secretly sent envoys to Hague Peace Conference seeking international support. The plan failed, Japan forced Gojong to abdicate.

events.title: An Jung-geun Assassinates Itō Hirobumi
events.description: Korean independence activist An Jung-geun shot Japanese statesman Itō Hirobumi at Harbin Station. An became Korean national hero, but this accelerated Japan's annexation of Korea.

events.title: Japan-Korea Annexation
events.description: Japan forced Korea to sign the Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty, formally annexing Korea. The Joseon Dynasty fell, and Korea began 35 years of Japanese colonial rule.

events.title: Japan Annexes Korea
events.description: Japan forced Korea to sign Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty, formally annexing Korea. Korean Empire ended, beginning 35 years of Japanese colonial rule.

events.title: March 1st Independence Movement
events.description: Koreans launched a massive independence movement, reading the Declaration of Independence. Japanese colonial authorities brutally suppressed it, but the movement awakened Korean national consciousness. March 1st became Korea's National Day.

events.title: March 1st Movement
events.description: Koreans launched nationwide independence movement, declaring independence and peacefully demonstrating. Though Japanese violently suppressed it, the movement inspired global anti-colonial movements.

events.title: Provisional Government Established
events.description: Korean Provisional Government was established in Shanghai with Syngman Rhee as president. The provisional government led independence movement during Japanese occupation.

events.title: Yun Bong-gil's Hongkou Park Bombing
events.description: Independence activist Yun Bong-gil threw bomb at Japanese military officials at Hongkou Park, Shanghai, killing multiple high-ranking officers. This operation shocked Japan.

events.title: Liberation
events.description: Japan surrendered, and Korea gained independence from Japanese colonial rule. However, the Korean Peninsula was occupied by the US and USSR, divided at the 38th parallel. This day became Korea's Liberation Day.

events.title: Liberation from Japanese Rule
events.description: Japan announced unconditional surrender, Korea gained liberation. August 15 became Korea's Liberation Day. However, Korean Peninsula was divided by US and USSR at 38th parallel.

events.title: Republic of Korea Established
events.description: In the US occupation zone, the Republic of Korea was officially established with Syngman Rhee as first president and Seoul as capital. North-South division was formalized.

events.title: Republic of Korea Founded
events.description: Republic of Korea was officially proclaimed in southern Korea with Syngman Rhee as first president. September, North established Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Korean Peninsula formally divided.

events.title: Korean War Begins
events.description: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel and invaded South Korea, starting the Korean War. UN forces (primarily US troops) supported South Korea, while Chinese People's Volunteers supported North Korea. The war resulted in millions of deaths.

events.title: Korean War
events.description: North Korea invaded South, sparking Korean War. UN forces led by US supported South, China supported North. Armistice was signed in 1953, peninsula remains divided at DMZ.

events.title: Korean War Armistice
events.description: Belligerents signed an armistice agreement, with the border near the 38th parallel. The Korean War ended, but the peninsula remains divided, with both sides technically still at war.

events.title: April 19 Revolution
events.description: Student-led democratic movement overthrew Syngman Rhee's authoritarian rule. This was Korea's first successful democratic movement.

events.title: May 16 Coup
events.description: General Park Chung-hee led military coup, seizing power. Park ruled Korea for 18 years, implementing authoritarian rule while promoting rapid economic development.

events.title: Korea-Japan Normalization Treaty
events.description: South Korea and Japan signed treaty normalizing diplomatic relations. Though controversial domestically, the treaty brought Japanese economic support, promoting Korean industrialization.

events.title: Miracle on the Han River
events.description: Korea experienced rapid economic growth, termed the 'Miracle on the Han River.' Heavy and chemical industries developed rapidly, transforming Korea from an agricultural to an industrial nation.

events.title: Miracle on Han River
events.description: Korean economy achieved rapid growth, called 'Miracle on Han River.' Heavy and chemical industries developed rapidly, Korea transformed from agricultural to industrial nation.

events.title: Park Chung-hee Assassinated
events.description: President Park Chung-hee was assassinated by KCIA director Kim Jae-gyu, ending 18-year rule. Korea entered political turmoil.

events.title: Gwangju Uprising
events.description: Gwangju citizens rose up demanding democracy, military violently suppressed uprising. Gwangju Uprising became symbol of Korean democratic movement.

events.title: June Democracy Movement
events.description: Massive democratic protests erupted nationwide, forcing military government to accept direct presidential elections. This was turning point for Korean democratization.

events.title: Seoul Olympics
events.description: Seoul successfully hosted the 24th Summer Olympic Games, showcasing Korea's economic development and democratization achievements. This was an important Olympics with East and West participating together during the late Cold War.

events.title: Asian Financial Crisis
events.description: Korea was severely hit by Asian financial crisis, nearly declaring national bankruptcy. IMF provided bailout, Korea implemented painful economic reforms.

events.title: First Inter-Korean Summit
events.description: President Kim Dae-jung visited Pyongyang for historic summit talks with Kim Jong-il, issuing the June 15 Joint Declaration. Kim Dae-jung received the Nobel Peace Prize for this achievement.

events.title: Korea-Japan World Cup
events.description: Korea and Japan co-hosted FIFA World Cup. Korean team reached semifinals, sparking nationwide excitement. This enhanced Korea's international image.

events.title: Candlelight Revolution
events.description: Millions participated in peaceful candlelight protests demanding President Park Geun-hye's resignation. Park was impeached and removed, demonstrating mature democracy.

events.title: Panmunjom Inter-Korean Summit
events.description: President Moon Jae-in met with Kim Jong-un at Panmunjom, signing the Panmunjom Declaration. This was the third inter-Korean summit in 11 years, easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula.
